topline.text: A genuinely quiet 48 hours nationally - no new DfE, Ofsted or safeguarding announcements since the weekend.

Locally, Sheffield's finance and performance committee met yesterday to decide on £602k of funding for SEND-places expansions at Firth Park and Parkwood academies - no outcome had surfaced publicly by this morning.
topline.action: Worth checking with the council or Lift Schools if either is a feeder or partner.

topline.text: Reminder: Sheffield schools break for autumn half term from Monday (26-30 October).

diary.text: South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority Board meets.
NEU's formal strike ballot over pay, funding and workload closes.

items.lede: Firth Park and Parkwood expansion goes to committee.
items.body: Sheffield's finance and performance committee met yesterday to approve passing £602,000 of government funding to Lift Schools, part of a £701,312 scheme giving Firth Park Academy three SEND rooms and 30 extra Year 7 places (240 to 270), bundled with a temporary expansion at Parkwood Academy. Both respond to a projected Year 7 places shortfall in 2027/28-2028/29. The committee's decision hadn't been reported publicly as of this morning.
items.action: Worth a line to SLT if either school is a feeder or partner - check back for the outcome.

box.text: Share of pupils in state-funded schools recorded as disadvantaged at the end of Key Stage 4 in 2025/26, up from 28.2% the year before - DfE attributes most of the rise to Universal Credit transitional protections. The provisional disadvantage attainment gap index narrowed slightly, to 3.82 from 3.92.
box.attribution: DfE, Key Stage 4 performance 2025/26 (published 15 Oct, provisional)
